Title: MachineCare
Body:
Maintenance visibility for DIMM and AOI lines

Working local pilot | Representative equipment and component data

Decision requested: approve a scoped validation pilot and IT review.
Notes: Introduce this as a working local pilot, not a production deployment. The component references come from maintenance; inventory, cost and planning assumptions are clearly marked.

Title: One record from request to replacement
Body:
Equipment context  >  Part request  >  Review / reservation

Physical completion  >  Stock deduction  >  Traceable history

Shared inventory and purchasing give maintenance leads a common view.
No downtime, savings or ROI claim has been measured yet.
Notes: Explain that approving work reserves parts; only physical completion deducts stock. The pilot is intended to validate usefulness, not claim quantified savings.

Title: The line model now reflects your layout
Body:
EACH LINE:     DIMM PRESS 1   +   DIMM PRESS 2   +   AOI

B01 / L01       2 DIMM presses       1 AOI
B01 / L02       2 DIMM presses       1 AOI
B03 / L02       2 DIMM presses       1 AOI

6 DIMM + 3 AOI across 3 configured lines. Existing ACOS and conveyor retained: 11 total assets.
Notes: These are the three configured lines, not a claim that all nine building records have complete equipment. New tags, positions and operating statuses are demo placeholders; asset serials still need confirmation.

Title: DIMM catalog: ten supplied references
Body:
Load cell / cylinders / solenoid / reed switches / optical sensors
Manufacturers supplied: Delta Transducers, Airtac and Panasonic

Example: Finger cylinder | HFD12X50 | 4 used per DIMM
Load cell: serial reference 2511231, not a general part number

122 illustrative opening spare units across the ten DIMM entries.
Installed quantities and shared spare balances are separate.
Notes: Show HFD12X50 in Inventory. Two DIMMs imply eight finger cylinders installed per line; that is not the spare inventory. Tray clamp manufacturer remains unknown.

Title: AOI: robot cell and safety components
Body:
TM robot                         Model not supplied | 1 per AOI confirmed
PILZ small light curtain       PSEN op113H-s-30-030 | 4 per AOI
PILZ large light curtain       PESN op113H-s-30-075 | 2 per AOI
PILZ PLC PNOZ m bo.1         Ident-772104 | 1 per AOI confirmed

Identifiers preserved exactly as supplied. Validate against nameplates.
Catalog entries do not validate safety functions or inspection intervals.
Notes: PESN and PNOZ m bo.1 are retained exactly as received, without guessing a corrected model. Counts of four and two were supplied. The user confirmed one robot and one PLC per AOI.

Title: AOI: signaling, power and enclosure
Body:
Tower light                 ASTLF-110-4-5FT-CM | 2 per AOI
Switching supply          s-120-24 | 1 per AOI confirmed
VEVOR control box        Serial 240108586510146 | 1 per AOI confirmed

Tower-light and power-supply manufacturers remain unknown.
Control-box serial is a reference, not every AOI's asset serial.
Seven AOI catalog entries; 14 illustrative opening spare units.
Notes: Include the robot as one of the seven catalog entries. All seven have two illustrative spare units for the demo; no physical spare count was supplied. Do not describe a robot as actually in stores.

Title: Known information versus demo assumptions
Body:
SUPPLIED: component names, stated manufacturers, identifiers and explicit counts
CONFIRMED: two DIMM presses and one AOI on each line

ILLUSTRATIVE: spare stock, reorder levels, new asset tags / station / status
UNKNOWN: actual prices, bins, supplier details, lead times and service intervals

$0 = unknown-price placeholder. 365 days = demo interval, not an instruction.
20 catalog entries total: 17 supplied component references + 3 earlier samples.
Notes: Financial totals are incomplete and must not be used for procurement approval. Serial references must not be replicated as unique asset serials. The application shows demo notices.

Title: Ten-minute live walkthrough
Body:
1   Equipment: show a line with two DIMMs and one AOI
2   Inventory: search HFD12X50 and PSEN; distinguish installed from spare counts
3   Demo copy only: request one finger cylinder and show reservation
4   Demo copy only: record completion, stock change and history
5   Show low-stock planning, order stages and a CSV report

Use the PDF fallback if the browser is unavailable.
Notes: Never rehearse fictional completion in the installed database. Sign in before the meeting, check all screens and verify a CSV in Excel. Supplier ordering remains manual; email is disabled. The disposable backend test is not a signed-in browser acceptance test.

Title: What works today
Body:
Scoped Administrator / Lead / Technician permissions
Equipment registry, shared catalog and compatibility
Requests, review, reservations, completion and historical snapshots
Stock receipts / adjustments, purchasing and partial deliveries
In-app alerts, audit / stock viewers and CSV generation

Backup and email-worker code exists; unattended services are not activated.
Notes: Administrator manages accounts and structure. Leads run operations within scope; technicians operate within assigned access. Distinguish code implementation from infrastructure activation.

Title: Production gates: platform and assurance
Body:
IT: approved hosting, HTTPS, service identity, access controls and secrets
Engineering: supported patched runtime / SDK and deployment testing
Security: identity / SSO-MFA decision, abuse controls and independent review
Operations: monitored startup services and protected off-host backups
Acceptance: authenticated browser workflows, concurrency and recovery tests

Current server is loopback-only. Production date depends on these gates.
Notes: Keep the current architecture for the pilot. A production server adapter requires agreement; a database migration or framework rewrite is not automatically required. Define backup recovery objectives and test them.

Title: Production gates: maintenance decisions
Body:
Validate physical stock, actual assets, bins, prices and replacement intervals
Confirm AOI model spellings and counts; obtain missing robot details
Decide multi-bin rules, backdating, emergency review and corrections
Approve email recipients / SMTP and supplier-ordering process if required
Agree support ownership, pilot scope and measurable acceptance criteria

Recommended owners: maintenance lead + IT/security + application owner.
Notes: These business rules are unresolved scope decisions. They may be deferred explicitly for a limited pilot; do not describe them as completed or set a production date before the decision.

Title: The decision for tomorrow
Body:
Approve a limited, supervised pilot on one validated line.

Name a maintenance data owner and an IT/security reviewer.
Agree success measures: traceability, stock accuracy and operator usability.
Review findings before expanding access or committing a production date.

Today: working local pilot. Next: verified data and user acceptance.
Notes: Ask for permission to validate the process and assign owners, not immediate company-wide deployment. Capture feedback and prioritize production gaps. Use the detailed readiness checklist in the handoff package.
